frontier.hypothesis: The genuine remaining PRE-RA residual is the loop-carried i*2 induction variable ($fp, s10's finding) plus the code==4 y-compare branch-topology mismatch (beqz+bltz+j vs bgez, s6/s7's C-level kill that is still open at the RTL/instruction-count level) — both entangled in the same 3-instruction gap, neither separately closable by any spelling tried s9-s15.
frontier.mechanism: loop.c strength-reduction (the s10/s11 finding: target maintains i*2 as a second, genuinely loop-carried counter incremented alongside i, not recomputed per-iteration) combined with jump.c/reorg.c's handling of the nested y-compare (>=0 / >=0x3E9 double-branch) that our single bgez-based form does not reach structurally.
frontier.next_probe: s12's loop-carried-idx2 rewrite was measured worse (banked rejected/loop-carried-idx2-worse.c) using a SEPARATE loop-carried variable; the untried form is initializing that second counter's INITIAL value directly from `start` (matching target's single pre-loop `sll $fp,$v1,2`) rather than from `i*2` inside the loop body, so the multiply happens ONCE before the loop, not per-iteration. Needs a structural or solver-modality session to derive the exact C shape (a second loop-control variable stepped in the for-loop's increment clause: `for (i = start, idx2 = start*2; i < start+2; i++, idx2 += 2)`), then re-run inverse_compose classify to see if the multiset gap narrows.

frontier.hypothesis: The code==4 y-compare's `if (y - hit1[1] >= 0) { if (>= 0x3E9) ... } else { if (hit1[1]-y >= 0x3E9) ... }` nested-diamond form is what forces our single bgez where target has beqz+bltz+j — an un-tried restructuring (e.g. a single `s32 dy = y - hit1[1]; s32 ady = (dy >= 0) ? dy : -dy; if (ady >= 0x3E9) flags = 5;` absolute-value form, or splitting the >=0x3E9 check into its own goto-based exit) might reach target's 3-branch shape without changing semantics.
frontier.mechanism: jump.c / combine.c's handling of a signed-magnitude comparison pair: our nested if/else emits a single conditional branch (bgez) selecting between two near-identical >=0x3E9 checks, where the target's compiled form apparently short-circuits differently (beqz then bltz then unconditional j to a shared tail).
frontier.next_probe: Read asm/funcs/func_80056CB8.s lines around the flags==4/y-compare tail (not yet read this ledger cycle in full) and m2c-reconstruct that specific sub-block in isolation to see what source shape m2c infers for the beqz+bltz+j triple, before hand-deriving C forms to sweep.

frontier.hypothesis: The reg 11/reg 65 spill pair (unchanged s13->s15) may be resolvable by NOT keeping the 0x1F8002B8 literal (or whatever currently occupies those pseudos across the func_80053614 calls) live across the call boundary at all — i.e. a source shape where the 5th argument is computed fresh at each call site from something already live, rather than shared.
frontier.mechanism: reload1.c: a pseudo with reg_n_refs spanning a CALL_INSN is a spill candidate; if the value can instead be trivially recomputed at each of the two use sites (it's a compile-time constant, so this costs nothing extra in real instructions — GCC already reduces `li $x,0x1F8002B8` to the same lui/ori pair either way), removing its cross-call liveness might let reload pick a different, non-spilled home.
frontier.next_probe: This is the natural, ALREADY-BASELINE form (the literal `0x1F8002B8` is written twice in source at each call site, not cached) — s15's classify confirms the baseline STILL shows the reg 11/65 spill despite this, meaning the spilled pseudo is something else (possibly `pt0`/`pt1`/`hit0`/`work`'s addresses, or `flags`, live across the call). Needs a solver-modality session (tools/ra_solver/inverse.py or a fresh -da greg read naming exactly which C-level value maps to pseudo 11 and 65) before any further C-level lever attempt — this session did not identify the spilled VALUES, only confirmed the spill still fires.
